extracted.intended_audience: Authors, reviewers, program committee members, and the AAAI community participating in AAAI-26
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and policy update describing how AAAI-26 will handle the unprecedented submission volume, maintain review integrity, match papers to reviewers, enforce submission policies, and communicate timelines and sanctions. Intended to inform authors and reviewers about procedural standards and expectations for the AAAI-26 Main Technical Track review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission compliance (policy enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers not fully compliant with submission policies will be removed from consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of non-compliance include missing PDFs, non-anonymized manuscripts, over-length papers, authors exceeding the submission cap, etc. The organizers explicitly removed submissions failing these checks before review and will strictly enforce submission policies at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy enforcement under scale
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of reviewing does not scale linearly with submissions; resource constraints necessitate stricter enforcement of review process policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of limits on storage, compute, bandwidth, workflow support, and qualified reviewer time, the conference will apply stricter enforcement of policies (even where flexibility was possible in prior years). Stricter enforcement may reduce past flexibility and can introduce short delays in the reviewing schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper–reviewer matching: algorithmic matching and bid-robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper–reviewer matching uses state-of-the-art algorithms with robustness checks against bid manipulation; bidding is only one of many factors in matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers state that 'unsanctioned mutual bidding has a minimal effect' on matching because bids are outweighed by other factors including area of expertise, content of past publications, and geographic diversity. Robustness checks are applied to guard against bid manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching factors: expertise, publication content, and geographic diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching decisions prioritize multiple signals beyond bids, including area of expertise, content of past publications, and geographic diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors are explicitly listed as outweighing bidding in the matching process. Given imbalances across subareas, the matching algorithm balances fit, fairness, and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise expectation and adjacency handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Given extreme submission volume and uneven reviewer distribution across subareas, some reviewers will assess papers that are adjacent to (rather than squarely within) their core area of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked for 'grace where this occurs.' The organizers acknowledge this as an operational reality while emphasizing efforts to balance fit, fairness, and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding review integrity: investigations and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference is actively investigating potential ethics issues in the review process, and confirmed violations will lead to consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences may include sanctions outside the current review timeline and far into the future. Ethics Chairs and AAAI standing committees for publications and ethics will pursue investigations and/or sanctions beyond the scope of the single conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-assisted reviewing tools to detect collusion
rubrics_metrics.description: An AI-assisted reviewing experiment is being used to detect and counteract collusion among reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers report 'promising early results' from these tools and indicate they will share a detailed report after decisions are finalized. AI tools are part of the integrity measures alongside human oversight and committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Committee scale and recruitment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program Committee (PC) was expanded substantially to meet demand, recruiting over 28,000 PC members, Senior PC members, and Area Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PC is nearly three times the size of AAAI-25. The recruiting process included reciprocal reviewers nominated by coauthors of submitted papers—i.e., reviewer recruitment incorporated nominations/reciprocal arrangements as part of scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reciprocal reviewers in recruiting
rubrics_metrics.description: The PC recruiting process included reciprocal reviewers nominated by coauthors of submitted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal reviewers formed part of the strategy to expand reviewer capacity rapidly; this is noted as a contributing factor to the large PC size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational resource constraints and impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: At the scale of tens of thousands of papers, reviewing systems face limits in storage, compute, bandwidth, workflow support, and qualified reviewer time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These constraints motivate stricter policy enforcement, scheduling delays, and efforts to expand the technical program and professional staff support to sustain future conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and timeliness expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process may run slightly behind schedule; organizers will continue to send updates to the review schedule and have published specific phase deadlines and notification windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key timeline items (abstract and full paper deadlines, supplementary material deadline, notification of Phase 1 rejections, author feedback window, final notifications, camera-ready deadline, conference dates) are given; authors should expect possible short delays and will be informed of schedule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathways to sustainability (process evolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers are considering structural changes to enable sustainable scaling for future conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideas include increasing year-to-year continuity, expanding professional staff support, and establishing a standing editorial board. Community input is solicited to shape these changes.
